subject: Console: Differential route economics investigation + action items
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Console: Differential route economics investigation + action items

Hey team,

Quick heads-up: over the last two weeks our Console telemetry is showing a noticeable rise in per-route unit cost for a small subset of routes (top 2% by spend). Latency percentiles are creeping up for those same routes, but it's not uniform — some tenants see only cost regressions without corresponding latency alerts.

I want a short, concrete investigation to untangle where the additional cost is coming from. Specifically, can we get:  
- a per-route breakdown that attributes token spend to model variant, quantization profile, and kernel selection;
- tail latency (p95/p99) by route and by model variant for the last 14 days;
- a short list of suspect call paths (e.g., large context prefix reuse, excessive reranking calls, redundant embeddings) with sample request IDs;
- a first-draft playbook for engineering/oncall that lists detection triggers and immediate mitigations (fallback to cheaper variant, decrease prefix caching retention, temporary rate caps).

No need for a complete analysis — a 1–2 page summary + CSV export with the attribution columns above is perfect. Can we aim for an initial digest by EOD Monday (2026-12-07)?

Marissa
Product Lead, Console Insights
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Console: Differential route economics investigation + action items

Thanks Marissa — important callout. Monica, can you take point on the data pull and initial attribution? Priorities: model-variant attribution + quantization/kernel mapping. Jasmine, can you prepare a minimal Console UI card that surfaces the top-10 high-delta routes (delta = cost change % over baseline) so we can iterate visually.

Proposed splits:
- Monica: per-route CSV export (columns: route_id, tenant_id, model_variant, quant_profile, kernel, tokens_in, tokens_out, tokens_total, cost_estimate, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, sample_request_ids)
- Jasmine: mock of a compact card and a drilldown link into the CSV\/playbook
- Marissa: confirm the detection thresholds we want (e.g., >30% spend delta and >$500/week) and whether we want tenant-level or route-level first.

Also please include any quick wins in the playbook header — we need mitigations that are safe to apply during business hours. Let's target a 30-minute sync Friday morning to review the first pass; if that doesn't work we can do Monday.

Thanks — soojin
Soojin Lee

Redwood Inference

> Quick heads-up: over the last two weeks our Console telemetry is showing a noticeable rise in per-route unit cost for a small subset of routes...
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Console: Differential route economics investigation + action items

Attaching a quick export and a short draft playbook. High-level findings (first-pass):

1) Attribution: ~58% of the incremental cost on the high-delta routes maps to model_variant changes — customers who recently switched from v1.8-q4 to v2.0-opt (more FLOP-heavy) saw a unit cost increase even when average token lengths stayed the same.

2) Quantization/kernel: ~22% of delta is correlated with fewer requests being served by quantized paths (we saw a spike in requests routed to non-quantized CPUs during a scaling event). Kernel selection is noisy; we'll need more kernel-level telemetry to be precise.

3) Call patterns: ~12% looks like duplicated reranking/embedding work — a handful of tenants invoke an embedding+rerank loop in their flow. Sample request IDs: RQ-20261203-AX12, RQ-20261204-ZF77 (CSV has samples).

What I'm attaching:
- console_slice_export_20261204.csv (CSV export, see top rows for sample request_ids and mapping columns)
- draft_econ_playbook_20261204.md (short mitigations and runbook)
- per-route-suspect-list.txt (top 50 route ids by delta)

Notes / caveats: the kernel attribution is best-effort — we don't have deterministic kernel metadata attached to every token today. I flagged INF-2319 for adding kernel id to the pipeline events (see link in thread metadata).

Next steps I propose:
- Short-term: enable canary fallback to v1.8-q4 for routes in the top-10 list; add a temporary 15% rate cap for the top-5 tenants by spend while we push the UX card.
- Medium-term: add kernel id and quantization-bucket to ingestion (INF-2319).

Attaching files as stubs below:

Thanks for the fast turnaround, Monica — very helpful. I reviewed the CSV and playbook. Two quick clarifications before we act:  

- Marissa: confirm we want the short-term fallback to v1.8-q4 for the top-10 routes (Monica's recommended list) — I recommend we include an automated monitor to watch for quality regressions (we'll tie to the eval harness).
- Monica: please open INF-2319 and add the kernel id and quant_bucket fields to the ingestion event schema with an optional flag so we can backfill for the last 30 days where available. Put the ticket in the "data infra" swimlane and tag "console-econ".

Jasmine: once you have a quick mock of the card, let's ship a dev-only flag so Platform can validate the CSV drilldown flow. Can we sync 12/08 at 10:00 PST for 30 minutes to confirm actions? If that works I'll add it to your calendars.

I'll also moderate a short executive note for Growth and CS so they understand the mitigation steps and why we may temporarily move some tenants to older variants. Draft will be shared after our 12/08 sync.

Thanks — soojin
